title: Stopping Severe Bleeding
hook: Severe bleeding can become life-threatening in minutes. Firm, direct pressure is the single most important thing a bystander can do — and you do it now, not later.
key_points: Call emergency services first for any heavy, uncontrolled bleeding.
Press firmly and directly on the wound with a cloth or your hands.
Keep pressing — don't peek; if a dressing soaks through, add more on top.
For a life-threatening limb bleed that won't stop, a tourniquet is a last resort.
General info, not a substitute for hands-on first-aid training.
content_html: Severe bleeding is a true emergency, and the good news is that the most effective response is also the simplest: firm, direct pressure right on the wound. The American Red Cross emphasizes calling emergency services and applying that pressure immediately, because rapid blood loss is what makes these injuries dangerous.
extra_html: The Red Cross approach is to call for help (or have someone call) and then press hard and directly on the bleeding site using a clean cloth, gauze, or even your bare hands if nothing else is available. Maintain steady, continuous pressure — resist the urge to lift the dressing to check, since that can disrupt clotting. If blood soaks through, add more material on top rather than removing what's there. For bleeding from an arm or leg that is clearly life-threatening and won't stop with direct pressure, a tourniquet applied above the wound is a recognized last resort. This is general information, not a replacement for hands-on training; for any serious bleed, call emergency services and get the person to professional care as fast as possible.

related.hook: Most household cuts and burns heal fine with the right first move — and knowing the few that need a doctor keeps a small injury from becoming a big one.

related.title: When a Symptom Needs a Doctor
related.hook: Most everyday symptoms pass on their own. The skill worth having is recognizing the red flags that mean don't wait — call for help now.

related.hook: If an adult collapses and isn't breathing, you don't need training certificates or rescue breaths — just two steps that can double or triple their chance of survival.

related.title: A Spray-On Powder That Stops Bleeding in Seconds
related.hook: A new spray-on powder can stop life-threatening bleeding in about one second by instantly forming a gel over the wound — even on deep, irregular injuries.

flashcards.prompt: A dressing on a heavily bleeding wound has soaked through. What should you do?

choices.text: Add more dressing on top and keep applying pressure
Remove the soaked dressing and start fresh
Stop pressing so the wound can clot on its own

flashcards.explanation_html: Removing a soaked dressing can disturb forming clots and restart bleeding. The Red Cross advises adding more material on top and maintaining firm, continuous pressure.

flashcards.prompt: What is the single most important first action for severe bleeding, after calling for help?
flashcards.back_html: Apply firm, direct pressure to the wound with a clean cloth or your hands, and keep it there continuously. A tourniquet is reserved as a last resort for a life-threatening limb bleed that direct pressure can't control.
